title: Bounded Run of the Verifier
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, let the codec mode be fixed, and let $y,u,u'$ be finite Boolean words and $B\in\mathbb N$. Suppose $|u'|=|u|$, the starting verifier accumulator is $st$, and the starting register values $v$ satisfy $v(r)\le B$ for every register $r$, $v(E)=v(Q1)+2|u|$, and $v(Q2)+2|u|\le B$. Suppose also that for every $i<|u|$, the bits of $y$ at positions $v(Q1)+2i$ and $v(Q2)+2i$ are respectively the $i$th bits of $u$ and $u'$, with out-of-range bits interpreted as false. Then the codec program has a finite run, staying at every time strictly before its endpoint in configurations satisfying its precondition and register bound $B$, from label $vTest(st)$ with registers $v$ to label $vDone$ with verifier state obtained by processing the zipped pairs of $u$ and $u'$ from $st$; the final registers are $v$ with $Q1$ and $Q2$ updated respectively to $v(Q1)+2|u|$ and $v(Q2)+2|u|$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols
The bound $v(r)\le B$ for every register
The first queried-bit agreement for every $i<|u|$
The second queried-bit agreement for every $i<|u|$
caveat: The claim uses specialized codec-program notions of precondition and reachability; these have been paraphrased as a bounded run.
